overview: Deutsche Börse Group is a vertically integrated European market infrastructure operator spanning trading (Xetra cash equities, Eurex derivatives, EEX commodities, 360T FX), post-trade clearing and settlement (Eurex Clearing CCP, Clearstream ICSD/CSD), fund services (Vestima, Clearstream Fund Centre), and investment management technology and data (SimCorp, ISS STOXX indices/ESG/governance). The company reports in EUR, is headquartered in Frankfurt, and operates across Europe, the Americas and Asia, generating revenue through a mix of transaction/volume-based fees, recurring subscription-like revenue (data, software, custody), and treasury/net interest income earned on customer cash balances and collateral.

business_model.summary: Revenue is earned across the full capital-markets value chain: trading and clearing fees (volume-sensitive), custody/settlement fees (asset-value and transaction-volume sensitive), software/SaaS subscriptions (SimCorp), index licensing and ESG/governance data subscriptions (ISS STOXX), and a 'treasury result' representing net interest income/margin fees earned on client cash and collateral balances (interest-rate sensitive, not an operating decision). Reported FY2025 net revenue without treasury result of €5,189m grew 9% organically; total net revenue (including treasury result of €837m, down 20% on falling rates) grew 3% to €6,026m. Management states recurring revenues reached ~63% of total and buy-side clients now contribute ~36% of revenue.

revenue_streams.name: Trading & Clearing (Eurex derivatives, EEX commodities, Xetra cash equities, 360T FX/digital assets)
Investment Management Solutions (SimCorp software, ISS STOXX index/ESG/governance)
Fund Services (Vestima fund processing, Clearstream Fund Centre distribution)
Treasury result (net interest income/margin fees on client balances)

business_model.customer_type: B2B/B2B2C — banks, broker-dealers, asset managers/owners (buy-side), clearing members, exchange participants, corporates, and increasingly neobrokers/retail platforms via B2B2C
business_model.geographic_mix: Primarily Europe (Germany/Luxembourg hub for Clearstream, Frankfurt for Eurex/Xetra), with growing activity in the Americas (SimCorp client growth) and expansion in new geographies such as Japan for EEX power/commodities

main_competitors: LCH (LSEG) and ICE Clear Europe in euro interest-rate derivatives clearing
London Stock Exchange Group (LSEG) broadly across trading/data/post-trade
SIX Group/BME (Swiss/Spanish exchange and post-trade, acquired former Qontigo index stake)
Nasdaq (commodities/power trading, index and data competition)
CME Group and ICE (derivatives trading/clearing globally)
Euroclear (international central securities depository, direct Clearstream rival)
MSCI, ISS competitors and other proxy advisory/ESG data providers
competitive_position.market_position: Leading European market infrastructure operator with vertical integration across trading, clearing, settlement/custody and data — a structure few competitors replicate. Eurex holds an estimated ~20% share by notional (~10% by ADV) of euro interest-rate swap clearing, the entrenched incumbent being LCH SwapClear; EMIR 3.0's 'active account' requirement is a regulatory tailwind intended to shift euro clearing onshore to the EU.

moat_factors.description: Owns trading venue, CCP clearing, and custody/settlement (Clearstream) end-to-end, which is difficult for single-function competitors to replicate and creates cross-selling and data advantages

moat_factors.factor: Regulatory licenses and systemic infrastructure status
moat_factors.description: Eurex Clearing and Clearstream are systemically important financial market infrastructures (CCP/CSD) with high regulatory barriers to entry under EMIR/CSDR; new entrants face lengthy authorization processes

moat_factors.factor: Switching costs in clearing and custody
moat_factors.description: Collateral/margin netting benefits, established legal/settlement relationships and operational integration make moving CCP or CSD relationships costly and operationally risky for banks and asset managers

Liquidity in Eurex derivatives and Xetra cash equities self-reinforces (best execution, tightest spreads); commentators note incumbent liquidity concentration (e.g., at LCH) is a headwind to Eurex's clearing-share gains despite EMIR 3.0

moat_factors.factor: Recurring, non-cyclical subscription revenue (SimCorp, ISS STOXX, data)
moat_factors.description: Software and index/data licensing provide a growing recurring revenue base that diversifies away from pure transaction volumes

moat_factors.factor: Brand/trust as neutral EU capital markets infrastructure
moat_factors.description: Positioned as the 'gateway to the European capital market' amid EU policy push for capital markets union/strategic autonomy

weaknesses: Treasury result (net interest income) is a meaningful, non-operational revenue swing factor tied to ECB rate policy, introducing volatility management cannot fully control
Clearing share gains in euro rates derivatives against LCH have been slower than hoped; large clearing members have ownership stakes in LCH, diluting incentive to switch
ISS proxy-advisory business faces ongoing U.S. regulatory/political scrutiny (state AG actions, SEC subpoena, Executive Order-driven agency reviews) that creates episodic legal/reputational risk
ISS STOXX and index/ESG businesses underperformed expectations in 2025 (soft index/ESG demand, FX headwinds from USD)
Integration risk from a heavy recent M&A cadence (SimCorp, ISS STOXX full buy-in, pending Allfunds) could strain execution and cost discipline

growth_drivers: Secular shift of European savings into capital-market products (pensions, retail investing) driving custody/settlement and fund AUC growth at Clearstream and Fund Services

Pending acquisition of Allfunds (announced January 2026, ~€sub-5.5bn depending on structure, expected to close H1 2027) would materially expand Clearstream Fund Services into a pan-European fund distribution champion
Full buy-in of ISS STOXX (General Atlantic's remaining ~20% stake acquired for €1.15bn, completed March 2026) consolidates 100% ownership of the data/ESG/index/governance business
EMIR 3.0 'active account requirement' pushing euro-denominated derivatives clearing from London (LCH, ICE Clear Europe) toward Eurex Clearing
Growing buy-side (asset owner/manager) client base — now ~36% of revenue — and B2B2C expansion into neobrokers/private investor platforms
SimCorp platform ("SimCorp One") cross-sell/upsell driving Investment Management Solutions growth and realized cost synergies (~€90m to date)
Digital assets/crypto infrastructure build-out (Crypto Finance platform, institutional crypto custody/trading) and cloud partnerships with Google/Microsoft

Treasury result inflection: after declining since 2022-24 on rate cuts, treasury income rose y/y for the first time since 2024 in Q3 2026 on higher rates/cash balances — a swing factor now turning into a tailwind
"Leading the Transformation" strategy (through 2028): targets 8% CAGR net revenue (ex-treasury) to €6.5bn and 12% CAGR EBITDA (ex-treasury) to €3.7bn by 2028, via organic growth plus selective M&A
Capital markets union / EU policy tailwinds supporting a unified pan-European capital market where Deutsche Börse positions itself as core infrastructure

business.description: Derivatives/cash equities/commodities trading and clearing fees are volume-driven and sensitive to market volatility, which can swing with macro/geopolitical conditions (e.g., 2025 saw muted equity derivatives volumes amid low VSTOXX)
Despite EMIR 3.0 tailwinds, LCH SwapClear remains the entrenched liquidity pool for euro interest rate swaps; large clearing members' ownership stakes in LCH blunt Eurex's incentive offers
Simultaneous integration of SimCorp, full ISS STOXX ownership, and the large pending Allfunds acquisition raises execution risk and could distract management or delay promised synergies
Multiple U.S. state investigations/lawsuits, an SEC subpoena for client voting data, and a politically charged U.S. environment around proxy advisors create episodic headline and cost risk

financial.description: New bond and convertible bond issuance in 2026 (€600m subordinated hybrid, €600m convertible) alongside the ISS STOXX buy-in (€1.15bn) and pending Allfunds deal will increase debt; net debt/EBITDA was 1.22x at FY2025 year-end versus a 2.25x rating ceiling, leaving headroom but less than before

A meaningful slice of net revenue (treasury result, ~€0.8bn guided for 2026) is a direct function of ECB policy rates and customer cash balances, not operating performance; past rate cuts were a multi-year revenue headwind
USD-denominated revenue (e.g., ISS STOXX/ESG) saw negative currency effects in 2025, and Allfunds/other cross-border operations add multi-currency exposure

regulatory.risk: Allfunds and ISS STOXX antitrust/merger clearance
regulatory.description: The Allfunds acquisition requires EU merger-control and other regulatory approvals; while shareholder approval and EU foreign-subsidy clearance have been obtained, full merger clearance was still pending as of late 2026, with closing targeted H1 2027 and compensation payments possible if the deal fails to close
Ongoing European Commission antitrust investigation into the former Eurex/HEX-Nasdaq cooperation remains unresolved

A U.S. court ruled in March 2026 in the Peterson II case ordering turnover of ~US$1.7bn of Iranian central bank assets held at Clearstream Banking S.A. Luxembourg; Clearstream is assessing appeal and coordinating with EU sanctions authorities. Separately, German cum-ex related investigations by the Cologne Public Prosecutor's Office continue

regulatory.risk: EU Capital Markets Union / MiFID / EMIR regulatory change
regulatory.description: Ongoing EU financial-market regulatory evolution (EMIR 3.0, potential further CMU measures, EU AI Act applicable to AI use in products) can cut both ways — tailwind for clearing relocation, but compliance costs and rule uncertainty persist

macro.description: Both higher and lower rate regimes affect the business differently (treasury result vs. hedging/trading demand); the Q3 2026 environment saw both the ECB and Fed raising rates amid Middle East-driven energy/inflation shocks, a reminder of macro volatility's dual-edged impact
Escalation (e.g., Strait of Hormuz disruption cited in Q3 2026 filing) drives commodity/FX volatility that can boost or dampen specific trading volumes unpredictably
2025 saw equity derivatives hedging demand suppressed by a steady US tech-driven equity rally with low realized volatility (VSTOXX), illustrating sensitivity to market regime

macro_factors.industry_outlook: European market infrastructure benefits from structural tailwinds: growing retail/pension capital-market participation, EU capital markets union ambitions, EMIR 3.0-driven clearing relocation to the EU, and growth in digital/alternative assets. Industry growth is viewed as secular (8% CAGR target to 2028) layered on top of cyclical trading-volume swings.
macro_factors.cyclicality: Moderate and two-sided — transaction/trading revenue is volume- and volatility-sensitive (cyclical), while custody, software subscription, and index/data revenue are more recurring and defensive; treasury result adds a distinct, largely rate-driven cyclical layer
macro_factors.interest_rate_sensitivity: High for the treasury result line (direct function of ECB policy rates and client cash balances) and for cost of debt on recently issued bonds; indirectly affects trading/hedging demand (higher rate uncertainty can increase derivatives hedging activity)
key_input_costs: Staff costs/compensation (including share-based compensation tied to share price)
M&A/transaction and integration costs (e.g., Allfunds-related expenses inflating 2026 opex)

recent_developments.event: Q3 2026 results: net revenue ex-treasury up 14% y/y to €1,415m; EBITDA ex-treasury up 19% to €760m; net profit to shareholders up 18% to €559m; six of eight businesses posted double-digit growth; FY2026 guidance raised again to >€6.5bn total net revenue and ~€3.9bn total EBITDA

Issued €600m subordinated hybrid bond (4.2% coupon, 2052 maturity) and first-ever €600m senior unsecured convertible bond (0.5% coupon, 2031 maturity) to fund growth/refinancing; completed a €500m share buyback (2.1m shares cancelled) and redeemed a €1.0bn 2023 bond at maturity
Treasury result rose year-over-year for the first time since 2024 (Q3 2026), confirming management's indicated 'inflection point' as rate cuts stopped/reversed
Completed buy-in of General Atlantic's remaining ~19.69% stake in ISS STOXX for €1.15bn, taking Deutsche Börse to full ownership and effectively ending the dual-track IPO/sale process for ISS STOXX

Allfunds shareholders approved the Deutsche Börse acquisition (>99.9% of votes cast); deal structured as a UK Scheme of Arrangement, still awaiting EU merger-control clearance; expected to close H1 2027
Signed binding agreement to acquire Allfunds Group, the leading European fund distribution platform, to combine with Clearstream Fund Services and build a pan-European fund ecosystem

Capital Markets Day: unveiled "Leading the Transformation" strategy (successor to "Horizon 2026") targeting €6.5bn net revenue ex-treasury and €3.7bn EBITDA ex-treasury by 2028 (8%/12% CAGR), with annual share buybacks becoming a regular capital-return tool alongside dividends
Jens Schulte became CFO (effective September 22, 2025); Gregor Pottmeyer stepped down; Stephan Leithner continues as CEO (since January 2025)
Planned IPO of ISS STOXX subsidiary did not proceed in 2025, incurring extraordinary preparation expenses, ultimately resolved via the General Atlantic buy-in in early 2026

Ongoing U.S. legal/regulatory scrutiny of ISS (SEC subpoena for voting data, multiple state AG complaints, state law challenges) and major Clearstream litigation (Peterson II Iran/Bank Markazi turnover order for ~US$1.7bn, under appeal review) remain unresolved overhangs

items.notes: Headline opex growth higher due to share-based compensation (tied to share price appreciation) and Allfunds deal costs; underlying growth still ~3%

Implies continued operating leverage/scale economies via 'OneGroup' efficiency program
Cost discipline target underpinning EBITDA scale economies

items.target: 30-40% of net profit, rising per-share dividend
items.notes: FY2025 dividend proposed at €4.20/share, +5% y/y; management flagged a 'new record payout' expected in 2026, with share buybacks now planned as a recurring annual tool

guidance.management_commentary: CFO Jens Schulte highlighted the 'broad-based positioning' of the business model, noting changing interest rate expectations boosted fixed income/funding markets and the treasury result (first y/y increase since 2024, confirming the previously indicated inflection point), while rising assets under custody and settlement volumes in Fund Services/Securities Services reflect a structural trend of institutional and private European investors shifting into capital-market products. Management expressed being 'very confident about the full year' after raising 2026 guidance for the second time.

bull_case: Rare combination of structural secular growth (European capital markets deepening, buy-side expansion, digital assets) with a scalable, vertically-integrated business model that is delivering EBITDA growth well above revenue growth (operating leverage)
Treasury result has inflected positively after several years as a headwind, now adding to growth alongside resilient organic momentum — removing a key investor overhang
EMIR 3.0's active-account requirement provides a regulatory tailwind to shift euro derivatives clearing from London (LCH) to Eurex, a multi-year share-gain opportunity
Disciplined, investor-friendly capital allocation: rising dividends (30-40% payout target), newly recurring annual share buybacks, and record 2026 payout expected

Accretive, strategically coherent M&A pipeline (SimCorp integration delivering synergies, full ISS STOXX ownership, pending Allfunds) expands recurring, buy-side-oriented revenue and strengthens the 'full value chain' moat
bear_case: Rising leverage from back-to-back acquisitions (ISS STOXX buy-in, pending Allfunds, new hybrid/convertible bond issuance) could pressure the balance sheet and crowd out further buybacks if integration disappoints or rates rise further
Clearing share gains versus LCH SwapClear have been slower than hoped; large bank-owned stakes in LCH blunt Eurex's ability to win share even with EMIR 3.0 support
Allfunds deal faces regulatory execution risk (pending EU merger clearance) with a long runway to a H1 2027 close, and compensation payment provisions if it fails

ISS faces mounting and politically charged U.S. regulatory/legal risk (SEC subpoena, multiple state investigations/lawsuits) that could result in costly settlements or business model constraints for the proxy-advisory unit

Trading/hedging revenue remains exposed to cyclical swings in market volatility and geopolitical shocks; a sustained low-volatility, low-rate regime would simultaneously dent both transaction revenue and the treasury result

Valuation reflects a well-regarded, structurally growing business (consensus analyst ratings mostly Hold/Neutral with price targets clustered €235-330), leaving limited room for error on execution of 2028 targets
